prose: The military spending ranking broadly tracks total GDP: the United States leads both, and the top five on defence spending overlap substantially with the five largest economies. The United States spends approximately 3.2% of its GDP on defence. {{overlapCount}} of {{firstYear}}'s top ten remain in {{latestYear}}'s top ten: {{overlapList}}.

The most notable disruption in the ranking since 2000 is {{gainerName}}, which rose from {{gainerRank2000Ord}} in 2000 to {{gainerLatestRankOrd}} in {{latestYear}}. Ukraine's defence expenditure increased from $6.8 billion in 2020 to $64.7 billion in 2024, a tenfold increase in four years.

prose: Among {{latestYear}}'s top ten, {{climberName}} recorded the largest climb over the full series, rising from {{climberRankFirstYearOrd}} in {{firstYear}} to {{climberLatestRankOrd}} in {{latestYear}}. Oil-exporting states account for a disproportionate share of the top-ten climbers, reflecting the link between per-capita income and absolute defence budgets in smaller, high-income economies.
China, which ranks 2nd in both total GDP and military spending, moved from 6th in defence expenditure in 2000 to 2nd by {{latestYear}}.

faq.q: Are these figures adjusted for inflation?
faq.a: No. Values are in current US dollars as reported by the World Bank. Changes over time reflect both real spending increases and US-dollar inflation; within-year rankings are unaffected.

faq.q: Why do some countries not appear?
faq.a: The World Bank publishes military expenditure for {{reportingEconomiesLatest}} countries with available data in {{latestYear}}. Countries with no reported value are excluded from the ranking.

faq.q: How often is this data updated?
faq.a: The World Bank publishes updated military expenditure data annually. This page is rebuilt from the latest release, retrieved {{retrievedAtHuman}}.

methodology: Figures are military expenditure in current US dollars as published in the {{sourceLink}} (indicator MS.MIL.XPND.CD), retrieved {{retrievedAtHuman}}. Rankings are computed among all countries with reported data for each year; countries with no reported value in a given year are excluded from that year's ranking. Because values are nominal, changes over time reflect both real spending changes and US-dollar inflation; within-year rankings are unaffected. Trajectory sparklines index each country's series to its own {{firstYear}}–{{latestYear}} range and are not comparable in level across rows.
